question.text:
The ions $\mathrm{O}^{2-}, \mathrm{F}^{-}, \mathrm{Na}^{+}, \mathrm{Mg}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Al}^{3+}$ are

isoelectronic. Their ionic radii show:

options.text: A decrease from $\mathrm{O}^{2-}$ to $\mathrm{F}^{-}$ and then increase from $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$ to $\mathrm{Al}^{3+}$
An increase from $\mathrm{O}^{2-}$ to $\mathrm{F}^{-}$ and then decrease from $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$ to $\mathrm{Al}^{3+}$

solution.text: Amongst isoelectronic species, ionic radii of anion is more than that of cations. Further size of anion increase with increase in -ve charge and size of cation decrease with increase in $+$ ve charge. Hence ionic radii decreases from $\mathrm{O}^{-}$ to $\mathrm{Al}^{3+}$
